findings.description: packages/happy-app/CLAUDE.md "Reconnect Replay State" section (lines ~150-153) describes the monotonic-no-op guard as attached to setLastSeenUpdateSeq and frames it as the mitigation for "an async replay handler [that] tries to write a regressing seq." That framing is now stale in two ways. (1) The diff introduces a second, deliberately NON-monotonic setter resetLastSeenUpdateSeq in packages/happy-app/sources/sync/storage.ts:1066-1079, which does NOT no-op on a regressing seq and instead writes whatever value it is given. (2) The replay-overflow handler at packages/happy-app/sources/sync/sync.ts:1648 was switched from setLastSeenUpdateSeq to resetLastSeenUpdateSeq precisely so the recovery path can move the stored seq backwards to the server's currentSeq after a daemon restart. So the doc's claim that "the async replay handler" is the case the monotonic guard protects against is no longer correct (the replay-overflow handler intentionally bypasses the guard via the new setter), and the doc never mentions resetLastSeenUpdateSeq at all even though it is now part of the post-overflow recovery contract.
findings.resolution: Updated Reconnect Replay State section in packages/happy-app/CLAUDE.md to document both setLastSeenUpdateSeq (monotonic) and resetLastSeenUpdateSeq (non-monotonic, replay-overflow only). Reworded stale framing.
findings.suggestedFix: Update packages/happy-app/CLAUDE.md "Reconnect Replay State" to document BOTH setters: (a) setLastSeenUpdateSeq remains the monotonic, no-op-on-regressing-write setter used by per-update persistence (sync.ts persistLastSeenUpdateSeq → applies to synchronous-apply branches AND the deferred-invalidate .then() tail-persists), which protects against out-of-order async handleUpdate completions clobbering a higher stored seq with a lower one; (b) resetLastSeenUpdateSeq is the non-monotonic setter used exclusively by the replay-overflow handler so it can reset the stored seq to the server's currentSeq after a daemon restart (when lastSeenSeq > currentSeq), even when currentSeq is smaller than the stored seq. Reword the "an async replay handler tries to write a regressing seq" sentence so it points at the per-update persist path (out-of-order handleUpdate completions) rather than implying the replay-overflow handler still goes through the monotonic guard.
